content: 1000% agree with Sutton here. Having worked in AI for over a decade (pre-LLMs), it's clear we need smarter methods for intelligence to truly compound in the way some of us envision it. To me, Transformers just scratched the surface. This arc is coming to an end; a new algorithmic paradigm is about to begin. The folks working on it are already quietly building. You just don't hear enough about them today. Some companies that heavily optimized for this arc will find out the hard way why that was a mistake. When I hear all the insane claims and AI fear-mongering driving most of the conversation around AI today, I constantly remind myself and others to go back to the science of AI: the algorithms, the foundations, the scientific rigor around measuring intelligence, etc. If you track research in this space, you already know the science is far from finished. Let's keep building. Brute force computation is not enough for intelligence. Clever new methods are needed. The science of AI is far from finished. IMHO

How GitHub is rebuilding for Agents 225M developers. 34.3B commits in a year. @github’s agent era is a full-stack rebuild—and @jayparikh, EVP of CoreAI at Microsoft, is leading it. https://youtu.be/rSWiNE92xqM Fresh off his GitHub Universe keynote, Jay goes deep on Copilot Fusion: breaking a task across models to improve quality, cost and speed, and how the harness and model orchestration improve together. We also get into the infrastructure behind agent-scale GitHub, carrying one session from phone to desktop, and a question every AI engineer should care about: how do you connect token spending to useful work shipped? Decrease the number of touchpoints with agents and instead improve the coordination with and among agents. Add a queue and a good memory system and watch how much faster and efficient you become. Any other setup from what I have tested in my custom harness will hold back agents powered by frontier models. I use this setup for coding, researching, strategizing, and much more. Increasingly, coordination and personalization are the key aspects of a harness that will give you the biggest edge. I've changed how I work over the last few weeks. I now have one lead agent for each area of focus, running all the time, and a chief of staff agent that oversees them. Each lead manages its own sub-agents that write code, test it, chase reviews, and coordinate with team members.…

Jeff Bezos reveals the simple phrase that saved him countless arguments running Amazon: "Disagree and commit is a really important principle that saves a lot of arguing." How it worked with his own team: "One of my direct reports would want to do something. I'd think it was a bad idea. We'd go back and forth and I'd often say, you know what, I don't think you're right, but I'm going to gamble with you." "You're closer to the ground truth than I am. I've known you for 20 years, you have great judgment." The part most managers skip: "At least then you've made a decision and I'm agreeing to commit to that decision. I'm not going to be second guessing it, sniping at it, or saying I told you so." "I'm going to try actively to help make sure it works. That's a really important teammate behavior."
